chunks: Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Ali ibn Yaqteen, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), said:

I said to him, 'Something has accumulated in my possession and remains for about a year; should I purify it (pay Zakat)?' He said, 'No. Everything upon which a year has not passed in your possession has no Zakat due on it; and everything that is not a mineral (rikaz), there is nothing upon you regarding it.'

He (the narrator) said, 'And what is the mineral?' He said, 'The silent carved [ornaments].' Then he said, 'When you intend that, melt it, for there is no Zakat in the melting of gold and the carving of silver.'

key_terms.الصَّامِتُ: The silent [ornament], referring to jewelry not used for trade
key_terms.الْحَوْلُ: The lunar year (period of holding wealth)

ai.seo_question: Is Zakat due on gold and silver jewelry kept for personal use?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the exemption of personal gold and silver ornaments from Zakat, a ruling that distinguishes between wealth held for investment versus that held for personal use. It clarifies that the obligation of a full lunar year (hawl) applies to accumulated wealth, while 'rikaz' (minerals/gems) and melted gold/silver used as jewelry are treated distinctly, reflecting the Shia scholarly view that Zakat is primarily on circulating capital rather than fixed assets.

en.hubeali:
Hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz, from Ali Bin Yaqteen, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ibrahim<sup>asws</sup> (7<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>), said,

‘I said to himasws, ‘Something has gathered in my possession, and it remained for approximately a year, should we purify it (pay Zakāt)?’ Heasws said: ‘No. Everything in your possession which a year has not passed upon, so there is no Zakāt in it; and everything what does not happen to be a mineral, so there is nothing upon you’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘And what is the mineral?’ Heasws said: ‘The silent carving’. Then heasws said: ‘Whenever you intend that, so cast it, for there would not be, in your casting of gold and a carving of silver, anything from the Zakāt’.
en.sarwar: 8. Hammad ibn ‘Isa has narrated from Hariz from Ali ibn Yaqtin who has said the following:

“I once said to abu Ibrahim, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, certain things accumulate with me and remain for about a year. Is there Zakat on it? He (the Imam) said, ‘No, Zakat is not due on it. Use whatever is with you until one is passed, Zakat is not due on it and whatever is not rika’z you do not owe anything therefor.’
I then asked, ‘What is rika’z? He (the Imam) said, ‘It is solid with designs on it.’ He (the Imam) then said, ‘If you like you can cast them because Zakat is not due on alloys of silver and gold.”’
